Definition: Eshcol, the name of an Amorite, also of a valley in Palestine
BiblicalUsage: ʼEshkôl was an Amorite, an ally of Abraham, and also the name of the valley where the spies cut the cluster. The name occurs 6 times, most often in Numbers. The fuller story lives on the People profile.
TheologicalSignificance: I take ʼEshkôl as it stands: a real name, in a real record. That is enough reason to slow down and notice the name rather than skip it.
RelatedEvents: The Twelve Spies and Israel's Unbelief; Abram Rescues Lot
